title: Bowling Plans as Optimization: Allocating 20 Overs for Gujarat Titans
dek: Twenty overs, five bowlers, four overs each: allocating them is an optimisation problem. Solving it for Gujarat Titans' attack shows how much the right plan is worth.
excerpt: Checking every feasible way to share twenty overs among Gujarat Titans' five busiest bowlers, the best plan saves a measurable number of runs against the average plan. The plan itself shows who should bowl when.
author: CricField Editorial Desk

sections.heading: Bowling as an Allocation Problem
body: A captain has twenty overs to share: six in the powerplay, nine in the middle and five at the death, with no bowler allowed more than four. Each bowler is better in some phases than others.
CricField took Gujarat Titans' five busiest bowlers since 2024, estimated each one's economy by phase (pulled towards the league average for small samples), and checked every feasible plan.

sections.heading: The Best Plan
body: Across {{ev:bp-count}} feasible plans, the optimal allocation concedes {{ev:bp-best}} expected runs, against {{ev:bp-avg}} for the average plan: {{ev:bp-save}} runs saved per innings.
The table shows the optimal overs for each bowler alongside his phase economies. {{ev:bp-death}} gets the most death overs.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
body: A handful of runs per innings is small in any one match but adds up across a season, and allocation is entirely within a captain's control.

sections.heading: What the Model Leaves Out
body: It ignores wickets, matchups against particular batters, conditions and the fact that a bowler's economy in a phase depends partly on when he has been used. It also assumes the same five bowlers every match.
It is a baseline for discussion, not a plan to follow blindly.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Plan the Overs Before the Toss
body: Gujarat Titans should start each match with a phase plan built on economy by phase, then adjust for matchups and conditions.
Measured against the average plan, the right allocation is worth runs every innings.

methodology: Built from the CricField warehouse (Cricsheet ball-by-ball data, regulation innings). Models are fitted on the warehouse itself and described in full here. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Phase economy shrunk towards the league phase economy with sixty balls of prior weight. Exhaustive search over plans with four overs per bowler and six, nine and five overs by phase.
